text: The $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Organelle}$ responsible for $\text{Packaging}$ and $\text{Modifying}$ $\text{Proteins}$ for secretion is the:
image: [Diagram of the Golgi Apparatus showing cisternae and transport vesicles]
explanation: The $\text{Golgi}$ $\text{Complex}$ processes, $\text{Sorts}$, and $\text{Packages}$ $\text{Macromolecules}$ like $\text{Proteins}$ and $\text{Lipids}$ into $\text{Vesicles}$ for delivery to other organelles or secretion out of the cell.

text: Which of the following is the $\text{Final}$ $\text{Product}$ of $\text{Anaerobic}$ $\text{Respiration}$ in $\text{Yeast}$?
image: [Chemical equation for alcoholic fermentation]
explanation: In $\text{Yeast}$ (a $\text{Fungus}$), anaerobic respiration (alcoholic $\text{Fermentation}$) produces $\text{Ethanol}$ ($	ext{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$) and $\text{Carbon}$ $\text{Dioxide}$ ($	ext{CO}_2$).

text: The $\text{Structure}$ that prevents the $\text{Backflow}$ of $\text{Blood}$ in the $\text{Veins}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of a vein with valves open and closed]
explanation: Veins carry blood back to the heart, often against gravity, and have $\text{One}$-$\text{Way}$ $\text{Valves}$ that ensure blood flows in the correct direction and prevent $\text{Pooling}$ or $\text{Backflow}$.

text: Which of the following hormones is directly responsible for the $\text{Maturation}$ of $\text{Follicles}$ in the $\text{Ovary}$?
image: [Diagram illustrating the effect of FSH and LH on the ovarian cycle]
explanation: $\text{FSH}$ is secreted by the $\text{Pituitary}$ $\text{Gland}$ and primarily stimulates the growth and maturation of the ovarian $\text{Follicles}$.

text: The $\text{Process}$ of $\text{Fusion}$ of $\text{Male}$ and $\text{Female}$ $\text{Gametes}$ in $\text{Flowering}$ $\text{Plants}$ is called:
image: [Diagram of Double Fertilization in flowering plants]
explanation: $\text{Fertilization}$ is the sexual reproduction process where the $\text{Nucleus}$ of the $\text{Pollen}$ $\text{Grain}$ (male gamete) $\text{Fuses}$ with the $\text{Ovule}$ (female gamete) to form a $\text{Zygote}$.

text: The presence of $\text{Scales}$ in reptiles is primarily an adaptation for:
explanation: Reptiles are adapted to terrestrial life. Their $\text{Keratinous}$ $\text{Scales}$ form a $\text{Waterproof}$ layer that significantly reduces $\text{Evaporation}$, helping in $\text{Conserving}$ $\text{Water}$.

text: Which of these is the $\text{Habitat}$ of a $\text{Tapeworm}$ ($	ext{Taenia}$ $\text{spp.}$)?
image: [Diagram of a Tapeworm lifecycle showing the human host]
explanation: The $\text{Adult}$ $\text{Tapeworm}$ is an $\text{Endoparasite}$ that $\text{Attaches}$ to the $\text{Wall}$ of the $\text{Small}$ $\text{Intestine}$ in its $\text{Primary}$ $\text{Host}$ (often a mammal, including humans).

text: The $\text{Term}$ used to describe the $\text{Position}$ an $\text{Organism}$ occupies in a $\text{Food}$ $\text{Chain}$ is:
image: [Diagram of a food chain showing different trophic levels]
explanation: A $\text{Trophic}$ $\text{Level}$ is the feeding position in a $\text{Food}$ $\text{Chain}$, such as $\text{Producer}$, $\text{Primary}$ $\text{Consumer}$, $\text{Secondary}$ $\text{Consumer}$, etc.

text: The major product of the $\text{Dark}$ $\text{Reaction}$ ($\text{Calvin}$ $\text{Cycle}$) of $\text{Photosynthesis}$ is:
image: [Diagram of the Calvin Cycle]
explanation: The $\text{Dark}$ $\text{Reaction}$ uses the $\text{ATP}$ and $\text{NADPH}$ from the $\text{Light}$ $\text{Reaction}$ to fix $\text{Carbon}$ $\text{Dioxide}$ and synthesize $\text{Sugars}$ (like $\text{Glucose}$).

text: If a tall plant ($	ext{TT}$) is crossed with a short plant ($	ext{tt}$), what will be the $\text{Phenotype}$ of the $\text{F}_1$ $\text{Generation}$?
image: [Punnett square for TT x tt cross]
explanation: Crossing $\text{TT} \times \text{tt}$ results in $\text{All}$ $\text{Tt}$ offspring. Since $\text{T}$ (tall) is $\text{Dominant}$ over $\text{t}$ (short), all $\text{F}_1$ offspring will be $\text{Tall}$.

text: The $\text{Gland}$ responsible for the 'fight or flight' response is the:
image: [Diagram showing the location of the Adrenal Gland on the Kidney]
explanation: The $\text{Adrenal}$ $\text{Medulla}$ releases $\text{Adrenaline}$ (Epinephrine) and $\text{Noradrenaline}$, which prepare the body for $\text{Emergency}$ situations (fight or flight).

text: Which of these is $\text{NOT}$ a characteristic feature of $\text{Monocotyledonous}$ $\text{Plants}$?
image: [Diagram comparing Monocot and Dicot leaves and root systems]
explanation: $\text{Monocots}$ typically have a $\text{Fibrous}$ $\text{Root}$ $\text{System}$. $\text{Taproot}$ systems are characteristic of $\text{Dicotyledonous}$ $\text{Plants}$.

text: The $\text{Process}$ by which $\text{Immune}$ $\text{Cells}$ surround, engulf, and $\text{Destroy}$ $\text{Pathogens}$ is called:
image: [Microscopic view of a phagocyte engulfing a bacterium]
explanation: $\text{Phagocytosis}$ is a type of $\text{Endocytosis}$ ('cell eating') where specialized $\text{White}$ $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Cells}$ (like $\text{Macrophages}$ and $\text{Neutrophils}$) engulf and degrade foreign particles.

text: Which part of the $\text{Eye}$ $\text{Regulates}$ the $\text{Amount}$ of $\text{Light}$ entering the $\text{Lens}$?
image: [Diagram of the human eye showing the Iris and Pupil]
explanation: The $\text{Iris}$ is the $\text{Coloured}$ part of the eye that contains $\text{Muscles}$ to $\text{Control}$ the $\text{Diameter}$ and $\text{Size}$ of the $\text{Pupil}$, thereby regulating the light quantity.

text: The $\text{Primary}$ $\text{Role}$ of $\text{Decomposers}$ in an $\text{Ecosystem}$ is to:
image: [Diagram of a Food Web showing Decomposers returning nutrients to the soil]
explanation: Decomposers (like bacteria and fungi) break down dead organisms and waste, $\text{Releasing}$ $\text{Essential}$ $\text{Nutrients}$ back into the soil and atmosphere for reuse by $\text{Producers}$.

text: The $\text{Function}$ of $\text{Bile}$ in the $\text{Digestive}$ $\text{System}$ is:
explanation: $\text{Bile}$ is produced by the $\text{Liver}$ and stored in the $\text{Gall}$ $\text{Bladder}$. It contains $\text{Bile}$ $\text{Salts}$ which $\text{Break}$ $\text{Large}$ $\text{Fat}$ $\text{Globules}$ into $\text{Smaller}$ $\text{Droplets}$ ($	ext{Emulsification}$), increasing the surface area for $\text{Lipase}$ action.

text: The $\text{Respiratory}$ $\text{Pigment}$ in $\text{Insects}$ is:
explanation: Most insects transport $\text{Oxygen}$ directly to tissues through the $\text{Tracheal}$ $\text{System}$ (air tubes) and therefore $\text{Do}$ $\text{Not}$ rely on a $\text{Respiratory}$ $\text{Pigment}$ (like $\text{Haemoglobin}$ in vertebrates) dissolved in the $\text{Haemolymph}$ ($	ext{Blood}$).

text: The $\text{Term}$ for a $\text{Genetic}$ $\text{Cross}$ involving $\text{Two}$ $\text{Pairs}$ of $\text{Contrasting}$ $\text{Characters}$ is:
image: [Punnett square for a Dihybrid Cross (e.g., RrYy x RrYy)]
explanation: A $\text{Dihybrid}$ $\text{Cross}$ is a cross between two individuals that are $\text{Heterozygous}$ for $\text{Two}$ $\text{Different}$ $\text{Genes}$ (e.g., $\text{RrYy} \times \text{RrYy}$).

text: Which of the following is $\text{NOT}$ a component of the $\text{Epidermis}$ of a plant leaf?
image: [Cross-section of a leaf showing epidermis, cuticle, guard cells, and mesophyll]
explanation: $\text{Palisade}$ $\text{Cells}$ make up the $\text{Palisade}$ $\text{Mesophyll}$ $\text{Layer}$ below the $\text{Upper}$ $\text{Epidermis}$ and are the primary site of $\text{Photosynthesis}$. They are $\text{Not}$ part of the epidermal layer.

text: The $\text{Excretory}$ $\text{Organ}$ of an $\text{Earthworm}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of an earthworm showing the location of the nephridia]
explanation: The $\text{Nephridia}$ (singular: $\text{Nephridium}$) are the $\text{Segmentally}$ $\text{Arranged}$ $\text{Excretory}$ $\text{Organs}$ found in $\text{Annelids}$ (like the $\text{Earthworm}$). $\text{Malpighian}$ $\text{Tubules}$ are found in $\text{Insects}$, and $\text{Flame}$ $\text{Cells}$ in $\text{Flatworms}$.

text: A major adaptation for $\text{Birds}$ that enables $\text{Flight}$ is the presence of:
image: [Diagram of a bird's skeleton showing the Keel (Carina)]
explanation: $\text{Pneumatic}$ $\text{Bones}$ are $\text{Lightweight}$ and $\text{Hollow}$, which significantly $\text{Reduces}$ $\text{Body}$ $\text{Weight}$ without compromising strength, a critical adaptation for $\text{Flight}$.

text: The $\text{Layer}$ of $\text{Forest}$ $\text{Ecosystem}$ where $\text{Photosynthesis}$ is $\text{Most}$ $\text{Active}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of a forest showing different canopy layers]
explanation: The $\text{Canopy}$ $\text{Layer}$ consists of the $\text{Tops}$ of the $\text{Tallest}$ $\text{Trees}$ and receives the $\text{Most}$ $\text{Sunlight}$, making it the layer where the vast majority of $\text{Photosynthesis}$ takes place.

text: The $\text{Part}$ of the $\text{Nervous}$ $\text{System}$ that controls $\text{Involuntary}$ $\text{Actions}$ like $\text{Heartbeat}$ and $\text{Breathing}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of the brain highlighting the Medulla Oblongata]
explanation: The $\text{Medulla}$ $\text{Oblongata}$ (part of the $\text{Brainstem}$) contains the $\text{Respiratory}$ and $\text{Cardiovascular}$ $\text{Control}$ $\text{Centres}$, regulating essential $\text{Involuntary}$ $\text{Life}$ $\text{Functions}$.

text: If a $\text{Food}$ $\text{Substance}$ turns $\text{Blue}$-$\text{Black}$ with $\text{Iodine}$ $\text{Solution}$, it indicates the presence of:
image: [Image showing a positive iodine test (blue-black color)]
explanation: The $\text{Iodine}$ $\text{Test}$ is used to detect $\text{Starch}$ (a $\text{Polysaccharide}$). A $\text{Positive}$ result is the formation of a $\text{Blue}$-$\text{Black}$ $\text{Colour}$.

text: The $\text{Process}$ of $\text{Shedding}$ the $\text{Exoskeleton}$ in $\text{Arthropods}$ is called:
explanation: $\text{Ecdysis}$ is the process by which an $\text{Arthropod}$ $\text{Sheds}$ its $\text{Cuticle}$ (exoskeleton) to $\text{Allow}$ for $\text{Growth}$. This is necessary because the $\text{Exoskeleton}$ is $\text{Rigid}$.

text: The $\text{Chemical}$ $\text{Substance}$ that $\text{Forms}$ the $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Wall}$ of $\text{Fungi}$ is:
image: [Diagram of a fungal cell wall structure]
explanation: The cell walls of $\text{Fungi}$ are primarily composed of $\text{Chitin}$, a $\text{Polysaccharide}$ that is also found in the $\text{Exoskeletons}$ of $\text{Arthropods}$. $\text{Cellulose}$ forms the walls of $\text{Plants}$.

text: Which of the following is an example of a $\text{Saprophyte}$?
explanation: $\text{Saprophytes}$ (or $\text{Saprotrophs}$) obtain $\text{Nutrients}$ from $\text{Non}$-$\text{Living}$ $\text{Organic}$ $\text{Matter}$. $\text{Mushrooms}$ (Fungi) are common examples of $\text{Decomposers}$.

text: The $\text{Process}$ by which $\text{Water}$ $\text{Moves}$ across a $\text{Selectively}$ $\text{Permeable}$ $\text{Membrane}$ from a region of $\text{High}$ $\text{Water}$ $\text{Potential}$ to a region of $\text{Low}$ $\text{Water}$ $\text{Potential}$ is:
image: [Diagram illustrating the movement of water molecules during osmosis]
explanation: $\text{Osmosis}$ is the $\text{Specific}$ $\text{Diffusion}$ of $\text{Water}$ $\text{Molecules}$ through a $\text{Selectively}$ $\text{Permeable}$ $\text{Membrane}$, driven by differences in water potential (concentration).

text: The $\text{Deficiency}$ of $\text{Iodine}$ in the diet of humans causes:
explanation: $\text{Iodine}$ is essential for the production of $\text{Thyroid}$ $\text{Hormones}$. $\text{Iodine}$ $\text{Deficiency}$ leads to the $\text{Enlargement}$ of the $\text{Thyroid}$ $\text{Gland}$, a condition known as $\text{Goitre}$.

text: Which of the following classes of $\text{Vertebrates}$ are $\text{Warm}$-$\text{Blooded}$ ($	ext{Homeothermic}$)?
explanation: $\text{Warm}$-$\text{Blooded}$ organisms ($	ext{Endotherms}$ or $\text{Homeotherms}$) are capable of $\text{Maintaining}$ a $\text{Constant}$ $\text{Body}$ $\text{Temperature}$ independent of the external environment. These are $\text{Mammals}$ and $\text{Birds}$.

text: The $\text{Primary}$ $\text{Function}$ of the $\text{Xylem}$ in plants is the $\text{Transport}$ of:
image: [Cross-section of a plant stem showing Xylem and Phloem location]
explanation: $\text{Xylem}$ tissue is responsible for the $\text{Upward}$ $\text{Conduction}$ of $\text{Water}$ and $\text{Dissolved}$ $\text{Inorganic}$ $\text{Nutrients}$ (mineral salts) from the $\text{Roots}$ to the $\text{Rest}$ of the plant.

text: In $\text{Man}$, the $\text{Process}$ of $\text{Gestation}$ is the period between:
explanation: $\text{Gestation}$ is the $\text{Time}$ $\text{Period}$ during which a $\text{Foetus}$ develops inside the $\text{Womb}$ of the mother. It spans from $\text{Conception}$ ($	ext{Fertilization}$) to $\text{Delivery}$ ($	ext{Birth}$).

text: The $\text{Accumulation}$ of $\text{Lactic}$ $\text{Acid}$ in $\text{Muscle}$ $\text{Cells}$ causes:
image: [Diagram illustrating Lactic Acid fermentation in muscle cells]
explanation: When $\text{Oxygen}$ $\text{Supply}$ is $\text{Limited}$ (e.g., during strenuous exercise), muscle cells switch to $\text{Anaerobic}$ $\text{Respiration}$, producing $\text{Lactic}$ $\text{Acid}$ as a $\text{Byproduct}$, which leads to $\text{Fatigue}$ and $\text{Pain}$.

text: Which of these is the $\text{Smallest}$ $\text{Unit}$ of $\text{Classification}$?
image: [Diagram of the Linnaean hierarchy (Domain to Species)]
explanation: The classification hierarchy, from broadest to narrowest, is $\text{Kingdom}$, $\text{Phylum}$, $\text{Class}$, $\text{Order}$, $\text{Family}$, $\text{Genus}$, and $\text{Species}$. The $\text{Species}$ is the most specific or $\text{Smallest}$ $\text{Unit}$.

text: The major $\text{Function}$ of the $\text{Root}$ $\text{Hairs}$ of a plant is:
image: [Microscopic view of a root hair cell]
explanation: $\text{Root}$ $\text{Hairs}$ are $\text{Extensions}$ of $\text{Epidermal}$ $\text{Cells}$ that $\text{Greatly}$ $\text{Increase}$ the $\text{Surface}$ $\text{Area}$ for the $\text{Uptake}$ of $\text{Water}$ (by $\text{Osmosis}$) and $\text{Minerals}$ (by $\text{Active}$ $\text{Transport}$ and $\text{Diffusion}$).

text: A $\text{Community}$ in $\text{Ecology}$ is defined as:
options: All the organisms of the $\text{Same}$ $\text{Species}$ in an area
The total number of $\text{Biotic}$ and $\text{Abiotic}$ factors
explanation: An $\text{Ecological}$ $\text{Community}$ is formed by all the $\text{Different}$ $\text{Species}$ ($	ext{Populations}$) that $\text{Live}$ $\text{Together}$ and $\text{Interact}$ in a specific area.

text: The $\text{Causative}$ $\text{Organism}$ of $\text{Malaria}$ is a:
image: [Microscopic view of Plasmodium in red blood cells]
explanation: $\text{Malaria}$ is caused by a $\text{Protozoan}$ $\text{Parasite}$ of the $\text{Genus}$ $\text{Plasmodium}$, which is transmitted to humans through the bite of infected $\text{Female}$ $\text{Anopheles}$ $\text{Mosquitoes}$.

text: Which of these $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Cells}$ are $\text{Biconcave}$ in $\text{Shape}$ and $\text{Lack}$ a $\text{Nucleus}$ in $\text{Mammals}$?
image: [Microscopic image of biconcave red blood cells]
explanation: $\text{Mature}$ $\text{Mammalian}$ $\text{Erythrocytes}$ ($	ext{RBCs}$) are $\text{Biconcave}$ $\text{Discs}$ that $\text{Lack}$ a $\text{Nucleus}$ to $\text{Maximize}$ $\text{Space}$ for $\text{Haemoglobin}$ and $\text{Oxygen}$ $\text{Transport}$.

text: The $\text{Movement}$ of $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Parts}$ in response to $\text{Directional}$ $\text{Light}$ $\text{Stimulus}$ is called:
image: [Image showing plant shoots bending towards light (Positive Phototropism)]
explanation: $\text{Phototropism}$ is a $\text{Growth}$ $\text{Movement}$ ($	ext{Tropism}$) of a $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Part}$ in response to the direction of a $\text{Light}$ $\text{Source}$. For example, shoots exhibit $\text{Positive}$ $\text{Phototropism}$.

text: In a $\text{Deuterostome}$, the $\text{Blastopore}$ develops into the:
image: [Diagram comparing Protostome and Deuterostome embryonic development]
explanation: Organisms are divided into $\text{Protostomes}$ (where the $\text{Blastopore}$ becomes the $\text{Mouth}$) and $\text{Deuterostomes}$ (where the $\text{Blastopore}$ becomes the $\text{Anus}$). $\text{Vertebrates}$ are $\text{Deuterostomes}$.
